_comment: INFORMATIVE — DATA RECAP. One config drives the script, the on-screen numbers, the durations and the footage per scene. Generalised from a production config; every project-specific value is a <placeholder>. Compile this from a tokenised template + a vars file (see _authoring) rather than hand-writing it. See references/formats.md §3b.
_startingPoint: A proven starting point, not a spec. The scene order, the kinds and the pacing worked for someone else's audience — tweak them for yours, one variable per experiment. references/formats.md covers running a format that isn't here.

meta.title: <slug-for-this-edition>
meta.concept: <what this edition found — the single most striking thing in the data>

_authoring._comment: THE RULE THAT MATTERS: never hand-type numbers into a config. They're only right for one edition.
_authoring.template: <workflow>/templates/recap.template.json — the copy and structure, with {{tokens}} where numbers go. Edit this to change the format for EVERY edition.
_authoring.vars: <workflow>/inputs/<edition>/vars.json — this edition's numbers, derived from your source data, not typed. Edit this to change ONE edition.
_authoring._why: A number that's right this edition and stale the next is worse than no number, and nobody notices until a viewer does.

brand: <the recurring name in the corner — this is a series, make it look like one>
accent: <hex — one accent colour for every number, bar and highlight>

voice.fallback: <a second voice id, used if the first errors — and then for the rest of the run, so one edition never mixes two voices>

settings.stability: <0–1: higher is steadier and flatter, lower is more expressive>

_gapNote: Silence added after each scene's speech. Small, but it's the difference between a recap and a machine gun.

scenes.vo: <the opening line — lead with whatever is genuinely most striking THIS edition. Never reuse last edition's angle.>
scenes.title: <the giant opening line. \n forces a break>
scenes.query: <footage that matches the mood, not the data>

scenes.vo: <one or two sentences setting the scale. Flowing prose — see the voiceover rule below.>
scenes.title: <what these numbers are>

counters.label: <what it counts>
counters.to: {{a number from vars, never typed here}}

scenes.clip_dir: <a folder of on-brand clips — a random one per render keeps editions from looking identical>

scenes.vo: <what the ranking says, in sentences. Do NOT read the bars aloud as a list.>
scenes.title: <what's being ranked>
scenes._barsNote: Only genuine, comparable categories belong in one chart. A meta-flag ('this repeats', 'unclassified') is not a category — charting it double-counts and buries a real one. Give it its own scene instead.

scenes.vo: <the one statistic worth remembering, and why it's surprising>
scenes.title: <framing line>
scenes.bignum: <e.g. '1 in 9' — one oversized figure, not a table>

scenes.title: <label for the list>

items.title: <the standout example in a few words>
items.desc: <one line on what it actually was>

scenes._authorFresh: AUTHOR THIS SCENE FROM SCRATCH EVERY EDITION by reading the actual source material. It is the video's originality — everything else is derived, this is the part a template cannot fill.

scenes.vo: <the CTA, spoken as a person would say it>
scenes.title: <the follow line>

_sceneFields.vo: the spoken line. Empty string = a silent card.
_sceneFields.seconds: force this scene to exactly N seconds — never cuts speech, extends if the VO is longer
_sceneFields.min: floor in seconds when not forcing; scene = max(spoken, min) + gap
_sceneFields.clip_file: your own footage — takes priority over query
_sceneFields.clip_dir: random clip from a folder each render — priority: clip_file > clip_dir > query

_rules: VOICEOVER: never write a comma-separated list in a `vo` line. TTS reads enumerations as clipped fragments with the pauses in the wrong places. Unfold anything list-like into sentences a person would say aloud. On-screen text may stay terse; the spoken line may not.
ON-SCREEN TEXT: no middle-dot or bullet characters as separators — use an em dash or rephrase.
Every number spoken or shown must match the source data. Recompile rather than edit.
The template is a scaffold, not a script: a fresh hook and freshly-authored standouts every edition, or the series flattens into a format nobody finishes.
Promote phrasings that worked back into the template so the baseline improves — without letting the baseline erase this edition's voice.
